name: Qwen3.8 27B AutoRound INT4, fixed-K batch-invariant profile, on two Intel Arc Pro B70 cards

library.summary: devan-carlin's AutoRound INT4 tensors served through vLLM's plain-GPTQ oneDNN W4A16 path with a rebuilt kernel library that pins a two-tier fixed-K GEMM strategy, FP16 linears in 32-row pieces, single-split attention and size-independent Inductor reductions, on the FP8 lane's whole-graph deterministic stack. Single-request output is repeat-exact and speculative decoding is lossless against the MTP0 oracle at every depth measured; MTP0 output is byte-identical to a single request through 64 concurrent users (a near-tie prompt can differ in some runs), speculative depths through 16.
library.benchmark_status: Research-status (2026-09-05, R239 matrix, TP2, final configuration): strict pairs MTP0 34.210/35.640 tok/s (G1 12/12), depth 1 51.098/50.088, depth 2 61.140/61.541, depth 3 67.613/67.831 (each pair 12/12 vs each other and vs the MTP0 oracle; depth 1 probe exact), depth 4 68.218 single arm (candidate b failed at engine start; re-run queued; 68.622/68.230 12/12 in R222). Identity ladders: MTP0 exact c1-c64 in three of four runs (998.6 tok/s aggregate at c64; one run c32 31/32, c64 63/64); depths 1-4 exact through c16 (650/522/599/516 tok/s aggregate; depth 4 one run c8 7/8), c32 30/32, c64 58-60/64. TP1 half running. No promotion or LocalMaxxing submission yet.

contributors.contribution: INT4 kernel routing diagnosis and gptq relabel, two-tier fixed-K oneDNN W4A16 strategy (rebuilt kernel library), FP16 row-chunk linears, batch-invariant attention and Inductor reductions, strict determinism/lossless/concurrency qualification on the R187 stack
contributors.validated_effect: The deterministic compiled TP2 work historically raised MTP0 from 18.910242 to 34.031596 tok/s, and block W8A16 separately raised matched target-only single/c128 shapes by 60.07%/29.30%. Clean-boot R119 qualified the draft-only INT4 R62 MTP1 profile at 54.424603 tok/s, 5.0504% above the prior qualified MTP1 profile, with both candidate and MTP0-oracle comparisons exact on 12/12 complete arrays in scope.

performance_profiles.label: INT4 fixed-K TP2 MTP0 identity-qualified aggregate decode vs concurrent users (c1-c64)
performance_profiles.scope: Measured vLLM HTTP completions on two B70s with the R224 image (fixed-K W4A16, FP16 row-chunk linears) and VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, no speculation, FP16 activations/KV, cache disabled, 128 returned raw token IDs per response on the 64-prompt small-context suite (R226). Every point is output-identity-qualified: each concurrent output equals its own sequential oracle byte for byte. One server, one pass per point; not a promoted concurrency speed record.

performance_profiles.label: INT4 fixed-K TP2 MTP depth-4 identity-qualified aggregate decode vs concurrent users (c1-c16)
performance_profiles.scope: As above with MTP depth 4 on the R228 image, VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 and Inductor split_reductions=false (R232). Points through c16 are output-identity-qualified; c32 (31/32) and c64 (63/64) were measured but are withheld because near-tie prompts took a different valid branch.
